name: KMacroExpanderBase::expandMacrosShellQuote
prose: KMacroExpanderBase::expandMacrosShellQuote(str, pos) scans str from index pos, tracking shell quoting state (single quote, $'...', double quote, $(...), $((...)), ${...}, (...) and {...} groups) on a stack, and replaces each macro recognised by expandEscapedMacro (when an escape character is configured and the current character equals it) or expandPlainMacro with its expansion quoted for the current context; str and pos are modified in place. When a macro hook returns a negative length the text is left as is and pos is advanced by the absolute length. An empty expansion outside quotes removes the macro text. Backslashes skip the next character. A backquote construct is rewritten into $( ... ) form: the opening backquote becomes '$( ', backslash escapes of $, backquote, backslash and (inside double quotes) the double quote are unescaped, and the closing backquote becomes ')'. A '$((' that turns out to be '$( (' is detected at the first ')' not followed by ')' and the scan restarts from the saved copy of the string and position. Return values: false at once, with pos at or beyond str.length(), if a backquote construct is not closed before the end of str; otherwise, when the scan ends, it returns true if the context stack is empty and false if it is not. The scan ends when pos reaches str.length() or on a ')' or '}' that does not match an open group of the proper kind (pos is then left at that character), so true can be returned before the end of the string is reached, and false is returned for unclosed quotes or groups. It takes no locks and the caller keeps ownership of str.
note: reviewers (original, round 2) right that unmatched ')' or '}' with an empty stack ends the scan and returns true (kmacroexpander_unix.cpp:231-241, 251); prose extended with the len<0 path and the $(( restart; the str.unicode()[pos+1] reads can run one past the end, not stated

name: KStringHandler::capwords(const QString&)
prose: KStringHandler::capwords(text) returns text unchanged if it is empty. Otherwise it takes strippedText = text.trimmed(), splits it on single U+0020 characters, passes the pieces to capwords(const QStringList&) (which uppercases the first UTF-16 unit of each piece), joins the result with single spaces, and returns a copy of text in which strippedText has been replaced by the joined string, so leading and trailing whitespace of text is preserved. Because the split is on every single space, consecutive spaces inside the text produce empty pieces, and so does a text consisting only of whitespace (its trimmed form is empty and splits into one empty piece); capwords(const QStringList&) reads and writes element 0 of every piece, so such input reaches an out-of-range access on an empty string. The input is not modified; the result is a new QString.
note: reviewer round 1 right: empty pieces from consecutive spaces / all-whitespace text reach str[0] on an empty QString in capwords(QStringList) (kstringhandler.cpp:29,40)

name: KStringHandler::capwords(const QStringList&)
prose: KStringHandler::capwords(list) copies list and, for each string in the copy, replaces its first UTF-16 code unit with str.at(0).toUpper(); the other characters are unchanged. The returned list has the same number of elements as list, and list itself is not modified. Every element must be non-empty: for an empty string the code reads and assigns index 0, which is out of range.
note: reviewer round 1 concerns callers passing empty pieces; the prose precondition already stated it

name: KStringHandler::perlSplit(QStringView,QStringView,int)
prose: KStringHandler::perlSplit(sep, str, max) returns a new QStringList of the pieces of str separated by occurrences of sep, skipping empty pieces. It repeatedly finds the next occurrence of sep from the current search position and, while an occurrence exists and (max == 0 or fewer than max - 1 pieces have been collected), appends the non-empty piece before it and continues after the occurrence. Afterwards the rest of str after the last consumed occurrence is appended if it is non-empty. So max == 0 means no limit; for max > 0 at most max pieces are returned and the last one holds the unsplit remainder; for max == 1 or max < 0 no separator is consumed and the result is str itself if str is non-empty, or an empty list otherwise. Empty pieces are not counted towards max. sep must be non-empty: for an empty sep the search position never advances and no piece is ever appended, so the loop (entered when max == 0 or max > 1) does not terminate. max must not be INT_MIN (max - 1 would overflow when max != 0). str and sep are not modified.
note: reviewer round 1 wrong: max == 0 is handled as 'no limit' (ignoreMax, kstringhandler.cpp:78,86) and the prose already said so; claim concerns max<=0 and max<0 only. Checked on all four perlSplit overloads

name: KStringHandler::perlSplit(const QString&,const QString&,int)
prose: KStringHandler::perlSplit(sep, s, max) forwards to perlSplit(QStringView(sep), QStringView(s), max) and returns its result: a new QStringList of the non-empty pieces of s between occurrences of sep, where max == 0 means no limit, max > 0 returns at most max pieces with the last holding the unsplit remainder, and max == 1 or max < 0 consumes no separator, giving s itself if non-empty or an empty list otherwise. sep must be non-empty (otherwise the search does not advance) and max must not be INT_MIN. Neither argument is modified.
note: reviewer round 1 wrong, same reason as the QStringView overload

name: KStringHandler::perlSplit(const QChar&,const QString&,int)
prose: KStringHandler::perlSplit(sep, str, max) forwards to perlSplit(QStringView(&sep, 1), QStringView(str), max) and returns its result: a new QStringList of the non-empty pieces of str between occurrences of the single character sep, where max == 0 means no limit, max > 0 returns at most max pieces with the last holding the unsplit remainder, and max == 1 or max < 0 consumes no separator, giving str itself if non-empty or an empty list otherwise. max must not be INT_MIN. Neither argument is modified.

name: KStringHandler::perlSplit(const QRegularExpression&,const QString&,int)
prose: KStringHandler::perlSplit(sep, str, max) returns an empty list at once if str is empty. Otherwise it copies sep into a local QRegularExpression and calls setPatternOptions(UseUnicodePropertiesOption) on the copy, which replaces whatever pattern options sep had (sep itself is not changed). It iterates over the global matches of the copy in str; while there is a match and (max == 0 or fewer than max - 1 pieces were collected) it appends the non-empty text between the end of the previous match and the start of this match and continues after the match. Afterwards the text after the last consumed match is appended if it is non-empty. max == 0 means no limit, max > 0 returns at most max pieces with the last holding the unsplit remainder, and max == 1 or max < 0 consumes no match, giving a one-element list holding str. Empty pieces are not counted towards max. max must not be INT_MIN. str is not modified.
note: reviewer round 1 wrong (max == 0 handled as no limit, kstringhandler.cpp:121,134); added that options of sep are replaced

name: KTextToHTMLHelper::atUrl
prose: KTextToHTMLHelper::atUrl() const reports whether the text at position mPos in mText starts a URL; it modifies nothing. If mPos > 0 and the character before it (mText.at(mPos - 1)) is a letter or digit or one of the dot-atom characters .!#$%&'*+-/=?^_`{|}~ it returns false. Otherwise it returns true if the text from mPos begins with one of http://, https://, vnc://, fish://, ftp://, ftps://, sftp://, smb://, irc://, ircs://, mailto:, www., ftp., file://, news:, tel: or xmpp:, and false if it begins with none of them.
note: checked prefix list and special-character list against ktexttohtml.cpp:170-201; prose was correct

name: KTextToHTMLHelper::isEmptyUrl
prose: KTextToHTMLHelper::isEmptyUrl(url) const returns true if url is empty or is exactly one of the strings http://, https://, fish://, ftp://, ftps://, sftp://, smb://, vnc://, irc://, ircs://, mailto, mailto:, www, ftp, news:, news://, tel, tel: or xmpp: (a bare scheme with nothing after it); it returns false for every other string. The comparison is exact and case-sensitive, and nothing is modified.
note: checked against ktexttohtml.cpp:205-229; prose was correct

name: ConnectionBackend::waitForIncomingTask
prose: ConnectionBackend::waitForIncomingTask(ms) waits until one complete command has been received from the worker socket or until ms milliseconds have passed (ms == -1 waits without a time limit); it returns true when a complete command was emitted from socketReadyRead (signalEmitted was set) and false otherwise. The state must be Connected and socket non-null (Q_ASSERTs). If the socket is not in the connected state on entry, it sets state to Idle and returns false without touching signalEmitted. Otherwise it sets signalEmitted = false and, if bytes are already available, calls socketReadyRead(); if that emitted a command it returns true. If not, it loops, calling socket->waitForReadyRead with the remaining time, while the socket is connected, no command has been emitted and the time limit has not expired, leaving the loop when waitForReadyRead returns false. After the loop it returns true if signalEmitted is set; otherwise it sets state to Idle if the socket is no longer connected and returns false (state stays Connected on a timeout with the socket still connected).
note: reviewer round15 right: signalEmitted is not reset on the early disconnected return (connectionbackend.cpp:135-140); round1 contract complaint not relevant to prose

prose: Generated function DataWorker::dispatch_sendMetaData() (macro DISPATCH_IMPL(sendMetaData) in dataworker.cpp, expanding to void DataWorker::dispatch_sendMetaData()); it takes no arguments and returns void. If the member _suspended is true it appends a QueueStruct of type Queue_sendMetaData with size set to -1 to dispatchQueue and starts the timer with interval s_kioDataPollInterval (0) if the timer is not active, so that dispatchNext() later calls sendMetaData(). Otherwise it calls the member function sendMetaData() directly (Q_EMIT expands to nothing), which emits the metaData(meta_data) signal; no error is returned and no locks are taken.

name: KIO::DesktopExecParser::resultingArguments
prose: KIO::DesktopExecParser::resultingArguments() const builds the argument list for launching the service's Exec line and returns it as a QStringList; on failure it returns an empty list (with d->m_errorString set) or, for a missing kdesu, a list containing just 'kdesu'. Failures returning an empty list: the Exec field is empty; the executable derived from the Exec line is not found or has no execute permission (error text says which); the Exec line has a shell syntax error (expandMacrosShellQuote fails); or the configured terminal emulator cannot be found, or the terminal command line has a syntax error. If temp files are requested and the application has no X-KDE-HasTempFileOption and there are URLs, it returns the kioexec path with --tempfiles, the Exec string, optionally --suggestedfilename and the URLs. With D-Bus support, URLs that the application cannot handle are mounted through KIOFuse; if a KIOFuse mount fails and some URL is unsupported, it returns the kioexec command line with the Exec string and URLs, otherwise it replaces the mounted URLs by their local paths. It then appends --tempfile when applicable, appends ' %f' if the Exec line has no URL/file specifier, expands the macros, and if the service wants a terminal it starts the result with the terminal command and '-e'. In the end the program is run as: with substituteUid, 'su' (terminal) or the kdesu helper with '-u' (otherwise), then the user name, '-c' and a command string that is either '/bin/sh -c <quoted exec>' when shell metacharacters were found or the joined argument list; without substituteUid, '/bin/sh -c exec' when shell metacharacters were found, otherwise the split argument list, whose first element is replaced by the resolved executable path when one was found. This slice shows only the last part of the function (from the KShell::splitArgs call to the final return).

name: DirectorySizeJobPrivate::processNextItem
prose: DirectorySizeJobPrivate::processNextItem() consumes the items in m_lstItems starting at m_currentItem, incrementing m_currentItem for each one it takes. A non-link item that is not a directory adds item.size() to m_totalSize and increments m_totalFiles; a link item increments m_totalFiles only and adds no size. For a non-link directory it calls startNextJob with the local path (QUrl::fromLocalFile) when localPath() is not null, otherwise with the item's target URL, which creates a recursive ListJob added as a subjob, and returns immediately without emitting a result (m_currentItem is already past that item). When the loop ends because m_currentItem has reached m_lstItems.count() (including when the list is empty or was already finished) it calls emitResult() on the job. m_totalSubdirs is not changed here.
note: reviewers right that links add no size (round 2) and that m_currentItem == count is valid and emits the result (original); directorysizejob.cpp:101-128

name: KIO::convertPermissions
prose: KIO::convertPermissions(permissions) converts a Unix mode value into a QFile::Permissions flag set. If permissions is greater than 0, each of ReadOwner, WriteOwner, ExeOwner, ReadGroup, WriteGroup, ExeGroup, ReadOther, WriteOther and ExeOther is set exactly when the corresponding S_IRUSR, S_IWUSR, S_IXUSR, S_IRGRP, S_IWGRP, S_IXGRP, S_IROTH, S_IWOTH or S_IXOTH bit is set; all other bits (set-user-id, sticky, file type and so on) are ignored. If permissions is 0 or negative, the result is the empty flag set. The function reads and writes nothing else.
note: slice cut the head; real name KIO::convertPermissions(int) (job_error.cpp:1285-1322); the prose omitted the permissions > 0 condition

name: KCoreDirListerCache::slotUpdateResult
prose: KCoreDirListerCache::slotUpdateResult(j) handles the end of a ListJob started to update an already listed directory; it returns void. jobUrl is the job's (possibly redirected) URL with trailing slashes stripped. Listers are collected from directoryData[jobUrl] (those holding the URL plus those listing it, after moveListersWithoutCachedItemsJob), and the list must not be empty (Q_ASSERT, compiled out in release builds). On a job error it calls jobDone(job) on every lister; when the job property _kdlc_silent is false it also emits listingDirCanceled(jobUrl) for each lister; for a lister left with no jobs it sets complete = true regardless of _kdlc_silent and emits canceled() only when not silent; then it removes the job from runningListJobs, calls processPendingUpdates() and returns. On success it looks up the DirItem in itemsInUse (if there is none it logs a warning, asserts in debug builds and would then dereference a null pointer later) and marks it complete; it compares the job's buffered entries with the cached items, skipping entries with an empty name or '..', setting the root item from '.' when none exists yet, hiding local files listed in .hidden, re-inserting items found to have changed (also those queued in pendingUpdates or pendingRemoteUpdates) and notifying listers with addRefreshItem, and collecting new items; it sorts the new items by URL, inserts them into the DirItem and calls addNewItems on every lister; removes the job from runningListJobs; calls deleteUnmarkedItems for the old items not seen again; then for each lister it calls emitItems and jobDone(job), emits listingDirCompleted(jobUrl), and when the lister has no jobs left sets complete = true and emits completed(). Finally it calls processPendingUpdates() and, if the job property need_another_update is true, updateDirectory(jobUrl).
note: reviewers round2 and original are consistent with the code: error path sets complete=true unconditionally but only emits canceled signals when not silent (kcoredirlister.cpp:1687-1696); prose checked line by line

name: KFileItemPrivate::parsePermissions
prose: KFileItemPrivate::parsePermissions(perm) const returns an ls-style permission string for the mode perm and the item's own state; the packet name KFileItem::permissionString does not exist (the public wrapper is KFileItem::permissionsString) and the slice cut the head of this inline function. It calls ensureInitialized() first, then fills a static 12-byte buffer shared by all calls (so concurrent calls are not safe and the result is copied out with QString::fromLatin1) and returns it as a QString of length 10, or 11 with '+' at index 10 when m_entry contains UDS_EXTENDED_ACL. Index 0 is 'l' if m_bLink is set; otherwise, if m_fileMode is not KFileItem::Unknown, 'd' for a directory, and on Unix 's', 'c', 'b' or 'p' for a socket, character device, block device or FIFO, and '-' for other types; and '-' when m_fileMode is Unknown. Indices 1, 4 and 7 are 'r' if the user, group or other read bit is set in perm and '-' otherwise; indices 2, 5 and 8 are 'w' or '-' likewise for the write bits. Index 3 is 's' if both S_IXUSR and S_ISUID are set, 'S' if only S_ISUID, 'x' if only S_IXUSR and '-' if neither; index 6 uses S_IXGRP and S_ISGID the same way; index 9 uses S_IXOTH and S_ISVTX and gives 't' if both are set, 'T' if only S_ISVTX, 'x' if only S_IXOTH and '-' if neither.
note: prior prose wrong in three places: index 9 uses 't'/'T' (kfileitem.cpp:518-526), the buffer is a static (492) not local, and ensureInitialized() is called (490) so members may be modified lazily; head at kfileitem.cpp:488
